rationale: The measured power spectrum is not distinguishable from a Lambda CDM realisation (Monte Carlo p = 0.295, 0.54 sigma equivalent).
summary: Using COSMOS clustered Lambda CDM mock (no real survey data available), the measured matter power spectrum over 19 wavenumber bins was compared against a sigma8-normalised Lambda CDM prediction. The Monte Carlo calibrated test gives p = 0.295 (0.54 sigma equivalent), classified as consistent_with_standard_model. The measured power spectrum is not distinguishable from a Lambda CDM realisation (Monte Carlo p = 0.295, 0.54 sigma equivalent). Injection-recovery of a known 20% feature: confirmed. This run used synthesised data, so it validates the pipeline rather than constraining the universe.
caveats: The analysis ran on synthesised data, not a real survey. No claim about the actual universe can be made from this run.
Systematic errors are enumerated but not propagated into the p-value; a full analysis would fold selection function, redshift-space distortions, and calibration systematics into the covariance.
Only one experiment in the suite has been implemented; cross-checks against independent datasets are not yet possible.
unresolved_questions: Does the conclusion survive a real survey with full systematics?
Does an independent pipeline reproduce the measured P(k)?

analysis_steps: Ingest the galaxy catalog (real survey data if available, otherwise a documented synthetic catalog so the pipeline runs offline).
Preprocess: convert redshifts to comoving distances and 3D coordinates.
Measure P(k) on a log k-grid via FFT of the galaxy density field, with per-bin Poisson and sampling uncertainties.
Generate the Lambda CDM (BBKS) prediction, normalised to sigma8 = 0.81.
Chi-square goodness-of-fit of the measured P(k) against the prediction.
Calibrate the chi-square by Monte Carlo over synthetic Lambda CDM realisations, so the p-value accounts for correlated P(k) structure.
Injection and recovery: plant a known 20% feature and confirm the pipeline detects it before interpreting any real signal.
Assess systematics: survey geometry, selection function, nonlinear clustering, cosmic variance.
Adversarial review: ask what else could produce this result.
Classify using the decision rule fixed in advance (Section 51 vocabulary).

monte_carlo.interpretation: A large Monte Carlo p-value means the measured spectrum is indistinguishable from a Lambda CDM realisation. A small p-value would indicate a genuine deviation.

injection_recovery.feature: Gaussian bump at k = 0.05 h/Mpc, width 0.01 h/Mpc
injection_recovery.conclusion: The pipeline detects an injected 46.4% feature at 5.0 sigma. Features at least this large would have been found, so the absence of such a feature is informative.

analysis.data_origin: COSMOS clustered Lambda CDM mock (no real survey data available)

galaxy_selection.description: The catalogue's selection function biases the large-scale power spectrum if the completeness is not modelled.
galaxy_selection.impact: Unknown without a survey selection function; treated as a dominant unquantified systematic.

shot_noise.description: Poisson sampling noise from a finite galaxy count.
shot_noise.impact: Shot noise is 2.000e+01 Mpc^3, sub-dominant where P(k) exceeds it.

nonlinear_clustering.description: The prediction is linear BBKS; real P(k) has nonlinear clustering on small scales.
nonlinear_clustering.impact: Affects k > 0.3 h/Mpc; 2 of 19 bins lie in that regime.

redshift_space_distortions.description: Peculiar velocities smear the radial direction; not corrected in this run.
redshift_space_distortions.impact: Biases P(k) at low k by a few percent on large scales.

cosmic_variance.description: Only one realisation of the universe is observed.
cosmic_variance.impact: Limits the volume probed: box = 400 Mpc with 3200000 galaxies (nbar = 5.000e-02 Mpc^-3).

look_elsewhere.description: A scan over models or estimators can inflate significance.
look_elsewhere.impact: Not applicable here: the test is a single pre-registered comparison, and no model scan was run.

systematics.notes: Unquantified systematics are not propagated into the reported p-value, so the significance should be treated as an upper bound on the evidence.

adversarial_questions.question: Is the result driven by a single wavenumber bin (a look-elsewhere problem in disguise)?
adversarial_questions.finding: The worst bin at k = 0.351 h/Mpc carries 68.8% of the total chi-square.
adversarial_questions.verdict: dominated by one bin; interpret with caution

adversarial_questions.question: Would pure noise produce a chi-square this large?
adversarial_questions.finding: Observed chi2 = 459.9; 95th percentile of the noise null = 887.6409866021846.

adversarial_questions.question: Would this pipeline have found a real 20% feature?
adversarial_questions.finding: The pipeline detects an injected 46.4% feature at 5.0 sigma. Features at least this large would have been found, so the absence of such a feature is informative.

adversarial_questions.question: How often does the detector fire on noise alone?
Was this analysis specified before the data were examined?
adversarial_questions.finding: Analysis plan registered at 2026-10-07T03:50:55.079977 with seed 42.

adversarial_questions.question: Does the uncorrected chi-square agree with the Monte Carlo test?
adversarial_questions.finding: chi-square p = 0.0, Monte Carlo p = 0.295. The naive chi-square uses per-bin Poisson errors only and ignores the cosmic sampling variance of a single realisation, so it understates the uncertainty; the Monte Carlo p-value is the calibrated one and is what the classification uses.
adversarial_questions.verdict: DISAGREE (naive chi-square expected to be overconfident)

adversarial.notes: The result survived adversarial review only if the pipeline was shown to be sensitive, its false-positive rate was low, and the analysis was pre-registered.
